comparison.objective: Candidate installs one rack rail at a designated unit; record levels an existing rack shelf by relocating one incorrectly seated pull pin.
comparison.physical_skill: Both require rack-hole registration and maintaining level support. Candidate adds long-rail bimanual handling, front/rear spring-prong latching, telescoping, and screw driving; record isolates and moves one pull pin while preserving three others and supporting the shelf.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate checks both post attachments, spring extension, same rack unit, correct screw holes, and self-support; record checks all four pins at level 2, shelf pose, untouched correct pins, release, and 1 s stillness.
comparison.reason: The shared rack-level concept is real, but the tested mechanisms differ: complete rail attachment versus corrective support-pin relocation. Candidate needs explicit rack-unit and leveling tolerances; absence of those details does not erase the mechanistic distinction.
